$comment: Project-level hooks for this repo. PROJECT-level and not user-level on purpose: the rule being
enforced is about THIS tree's tracked files, so a user-level hook would carry it into every
other repo the agent works in, where `git ls-files` names a different set and the refusal would
be about something nobody decided. Scope the enforcement to the scope of the rule.
editroute.py refuses to edit a TRACKED file from a Bash command — inline interpreters that open
a file for writing, `sed -i`, and redirection or `tee` onto a tracked path. It exists because
`scripts/subst1.py` and the editor tool were already the rule and the rule was broken in all 8
writes to one script in one campaign. Its witness is TestEditRouteHookRefusesBashEditsOfTracked-
Files in internal/testenv, which `make ci` runs; the hook's own behaviour is asserted there
rather than here, because nothing runs this file as a test.
settings.json is TRACKED (only settings.local.json is ignored), so this applies to anyone
working in the tree rather than to one machine.
